# [Quicksort 2 - Sorting](https://www.hackerrank.com/challenges/366/problem)
## Easy
<div class="challenge-body-html"><div class="challenge_problem_statement"><div class="msB challenge_problem_statement_body"><div class="hackdown-content"><svg style="display: none;"><defs id="MathJax_SVG_glyphs"></defs></svg><p>In the previous challenge, you wrote a <em>partition</em> method to split an array into two sub-arrays, one containing smaller elements and one containing larger elements than a given number. This means you 'sorted' half the array with respect to the other half. Can you repeatedly use <em>partition</em> to sort an entire array?</p>

<p><strong>Guideline</strong> <br>
In Insertion Sort, you simply went through each element in order and inserted it into a sorted sub-array. In this challenge, you cannot focus on one element at a time, but instead must deal with whole sub-arrays, with a strategy known as "divide and conquer".</p>

<p>When <em>partition</em> is called on an array, two parts of the array get 'sorted' with respect to each other. If <em>partition</em> is then called on each sub-array, the array will now be split into four parts. This process can be repeated until the sub-arrays are small. Notice that when partition is called on just one of the numbers, they end up being sorted.</p>

<p>Can you repeatedly call partition so that the entire array ends up sorted? </p>

<p><strong>Print Sub-Arrays</strong> <br>
In this challenge, print your array every time your partitioning method finishes, i.e. whenever two subarrays, along with the pivot, are merged together. </p>

<ul>
<li>The first element in a sub-array should be used as a pivot.</li>
<li>Partition the left side before partitioning the right side.</li>
<li>The pivot should be placed between sub-arrays while merging them.</li>
<li>Array of length <span style="font-size: 100%; display: inline-block;" class="MathJax_SVG" id="MathJax-Element-1-Frame"><svg xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" width="1.162ex" height="2.176ex" style="vertical-align: -0.338ex;" viewBox="0 -791.3 500.5 936.9" role="img" focusable="false"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><path stroke-width="1" d="M213 578L200 573Q186 568 160 563T102 556H83V602H102Q149 604 189 617T245 641T273 663Q275 666 285 666Q294 666 302 660V361L303 61Q310 54 315 52T339 48T401 46H427V0H416Q395 3 257 3Q121 3 100 0H88V46H114Q136 46 152 46T177 47T193 50T201 52T207 57T213 61V578Z"></path></g></svg></span> or less will be considered sorted, and there is no need to sort or to print them.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Note</strong> <br>
Please maintain the original order of the elements in the left and right partitions while partitioning around a pivot element.</p>

<p>For example:
Partition about the first element for the array A[]={5, 8, 1, 3, 7, 9, 2}  will be {1, 3, 2, 5, 8, 7, 9}</p>

There will be two lines of input:</p>
